[^n3245]All that my Father hath is mine: therefore said I unto you, that he taketh[^n3246] of mine, and shall shew[^n3247] you.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section XLVII
text: Section XLVII. [1] [^n3248]A little while, and ye shall not behold me; and a little while again, and ye shall [2] behold me; because I go to the Father. [^n3249]His disciples therefore said one to another, What is this that he hath said unto us, A little while, and ye shall not behold me; and a little while again, and ye shall behold me: and, I go to my [3] Father? [^n3250]And they said, What is this little while that he hath said? We know not [4] what he speaketh. [^n3251]And Jesus perceived that they were seeking to ask him, and said unto them, Do ye inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said unto you, A little while, and ye behold me not, and a little while again, and ye shall [5] behold me? [^n3252]Verily, verily,[^n3253] I say unto you, that ye shall weep and grieve, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your grief shall turn[^n3254] to joy. [6] [^n3255]For, a woman when the time is come for her that she should bring forth, the arrival of the day of her bringing forth distresseth her: but whenever she hath brought forth a son, she remembereth not her distress, for joy at the birth of a man into the [7] world. [^n3256]And ye now also grieve: but I shall see you, and your hearts shall rejoice, [8] [Arabic, p. 178] and your joy no man taketh from you. [^n3257]And in that day ye shall ask me nothing. And verily, verily,[^n3258] I say unto you, All that ye ask my Father in my name, he will give you. [^n3259]Hitherto ye have asked nothing [9] in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be complete. [10] [^n3260]I have spoken unto you now in ænigmas:[^n3261] but there will come an hour when[^n3262] I shall not speak to you in ænigmas,[^n3263] but shall reveal unto you the Father plainly, [11] in that day when[^n3264] ye shall ask in my name: [^n3265]and I say not unto you, that I shall [12] entreat the Father for you; [^n3266]for the Father loveth you, because ye have loved me, [13] and have believed that I came forth from my Father. [^n3267]I came forth from my Father, and came into the world: and I leave the world, and go unto my Father. [14] [^n3268]His disciples said unto him, Lo, thy speech is now plain, and thou hast not said one [15] thing in an ænigma. [^n3269]Now, lo, we know that thou knowest everything, and needest not that any man should ask thee: and by this we believe that thou camest forth [16, 17] from God. [^n3270]Jesus said unto them, Believe that an hour cometh, [^n3271]and lo, it hath come, and ye shall be scattered, every one of you to his place, and shall leave me [18] alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. [^n3272]This have I said unto you, that in me ye may have peace. And in the world trouble shall overtake you: but be of good courage; for I have overcome the world. [19] [^n3273]This said Jesus, and lifted up his eyes unto heaven, and said, My Father, the hour [20] is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son may glorify thee: [^n3274]as thou gavest him authority [21] over all flesh, that all that thou hast given him, he might give them[^n3275] eternal life. [^n3276]And this is eternal life, that they should[^n3277] know that thou alone art true God, and that he [22] [Arabic, p. 179] whom thou didst send is Jesus the Messiah.[^n3278] [^n3279]I glorified thee in the earth, [23] and the work which thou gavest me to do I have accomplished. [^n3280]And now glorify thou me, O Father, beside thee, with that glory which I had with thee [24] before the world was. [^n3281]I made known thy name to the men whom thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them to me; and they have kept [25, 26] thy word. [^n3282]Now they[^n3283] know that all that thou hast given me is from thee: [^n3284]and the sayings which thou gavest me I have given unto them; and they received them, and knew of a truth that I came forth from thee, and believed that thou didst send me. [27] [^n3285]And I ask for their sake: and my asking is not for the world, but for those whom [28] thou hast given me; for they are thine: [^n3286]and all that is mine is thine, and all that is [29] thine is mine: and I am glorified in them. [^n3287]And now I am not in the world, and they are in the world, and I come to thee. My[^n3288] holy Father, keep them in thy [30] name which thou hast given unto me, that they may be one, as we are. [^n3289]When I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: and I kept those whom thou gavest unto me: and no man of them hath perished, but the son of perdition; that [31] the scripture might be fulfilled. [^n3290]Now I come to thee: and this I say in the world, [32] that my joy may be complete in them. [^n3291]I have given them thy word; and the world [33] hated them, because they were not of the world, as I was not of the world. [^n3292]And I ask not this, that thou take them from the world, but that thou keep them from the [34, 35] evil one. [^n3293]They were not of the world, as I was not of the world. [^n3294]O Father, sanctify [36] them in thy truth: for thy word is truth. [^n3295]And as thou didst send me into the world, I [37] [Arabic, p. 180] also send them into the world. [^n3296]And for their sake I sanctify myself, that they [38] also may be sanctified in the truth. [^n3297]Neither for these alone do I ask, but for [39] the sake of them that believe in me through their word; [^n3298]that they may be all one; as thou art in me, and I in thee, and so they also shall be one in us: that the world [40] may believe that thou didst send me. [^n3299]And the glory which thou hast given unto [41] me I have given unto them; [^n3300]that they may be one, as we are one; I in them, and thou in me, that they may be perfect into[^n3301] one; and that the world may know that [42] thou didst send me, and that I[^n3302] loved them, as thou lovedst me. [^n3303]Father, and those whom thou hast given me, I wish that, where I am, they may be with me also; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before [43] the foundation[^n3304] of the world. [^n3305]My righteous Father,[^n3306] and the world knew thee not, [44] but I know thee; and they knew that thou didst send me; and I made known unto them thy name, and will make it known to them; [^n3307]that the love wherewith thou lovedst me may be in them, and I shall[^n3308] be in them.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section XLVIII
text: Section XLVIII. [1] [^n3309]This said Jesus, and went forth with his disciples to a place which was called Gethsemane,[^n3310] on[^n3311] the side that is in the plain[^n3312] of Kidron, the mountain,[^n3313] the place [2] in which was a garden; and he entered thither, he and his disciples. [^n3314]And Judas the [3] betrayer knew that place: for Jesus oft-times met with his disciples there. [^n3315]And when Jesus came to the place, he said to his disciples, Sit ye here, so that I may go and pray; [4, 5] [Arabic, p. 181] and pray ye, that ye enter not into temptations. [^n3316]And he took with him Cephas and the sons of Zebedee together, James and John; and he began to [6] look sorrowful, and to be anxious. [^n3317]And he said unto them, My soul is distressed unto [7] death: abide ye here, and watch with me. [^n3318]And he withdrew from them a little, [8] the space of a stone’s throw; [^n3319]and he kneeled,[^n3320] and fell on his face, and prayed, so [9] that, if it were possible, this hour might pass[^n3321] him. [^n3322]And he said, Father, thou art able for all things; if thou wilt, let this cup pass me: [^n3323]but let not my will be done, [10] but let thy will be done. [^n3324]And he came to his disciples, and found them sleeping; [11] and he said unto Cephas, Simon, didst thou sleep? [^n3325]Could ye thus not for one hour [12] watch with me? [^n3326]Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptations: the spirit is [13] willing and ready, but the body is weak.[^n3327] [^n3328]And he went again a second time, and prayed, and said, My Father, if it is not possible with regard to[^n3329] this cup that it pass, [14] except I drink it, thy will be done. [^n3330]And he returned again, and found his disciples sleeping, for their eyes were heavy from their grief and anxiety; and they knew not [15] what to say to him. [^n3331]And he left them, and went away again, and prayed a third [16] time, and said the very same word. [^n3332]And there appeared unto him an angel from [17] heaven, encouraging him. [^n3333]And being afraid[^n3334] he prayed continuously:[^n3335] and his sweat[^n3336] [18] [Arabic, p. 182] became like a stream of blood, and fell on the ground. [^n3337]Then he rose from [19] his prayer, and came to his disciples, and found them sleeping. [^n3338]And he [20] said unto them, Sleep now, and rest: [^n3339]the end hath arrived,[^n3340] and the hour hath come; [21] and behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners. [^n3341]Arise, let us go:[^n3342] for he hath come that betrayeth me. [22] [^n3343]And while he was still speaking, came Judas the betrayer, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude carrying lanterns and torches[^n3344] and swords and staves, from the chief priests and scribes and elders of the people, and with him the footsoldiers [23] of the Romans.[^n3345] [^n3346]And Judas the betrayer gave them a sign, and said, He whom I shall kiss, he is he: take him with care,[^n3347] and lead him away.[^n3348] [24] [^n3349]And Jesus, because he knew everything that should come upon him, went forth [25] unto them. [^n3350]And immediately Judas the betrayer came to Jesus, and said, Peace, [26] my Master; and kissed him. [^n3351]And Jesus said unto him, Judas, with a kiss betrayest [27] thou the Son of man? [^n3352]Was it for that thou camest, my friend? And Jesus said [28] to those that came unto him, Whom seek ye? [^n3353]They said unto him, Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus said unto them, I am he. And Judas the betrayer also was standing [29] with them. [^n3354]And when Jesus said unto them, I am he, they retreated backward, and [30] fell to the ground. [^n3355]And Jesus asked them again, Whom seek ye? They answered, [31] Jesus the Nazarene. [^n3356]Jesus said unto them, I told you that I am he: and if ye seek [32] me, let these go away: that the word might be fulfilled which he spake, [^n3357]Of those [33] [Arabic, p. 183] whom thou hast given me I lost not even one. [^n3358]Then came those that were with Judas, and seized Jesus, and took him. [34] [^n3359]And when his disciples saw what happened, they said, Our Lord, shall we smite [35] them with swords? [^n3360]And Simon Cephas had a sword, and he drew it, and struck the servant of the chief priest, and cut off his right ear. And the name of that servant [36] was Malchus. [^n3361]Jesus said unto Cephas, The cup which my Father hath given [37] me, shall I not drink it? [^n3362]Put the sword into its sheath: for all that take with[^n3363] the [38] sword shall die by the sword. [^n3364]Thinkest[^n3365] thou that I am not able to ask of my [39] Father, and he shall now raise up for me more than[^n3366] twelve tribes of angels? [^n3367]Then [40] how should the scriptures which were spoken be fulfilled, that thus it must be? [^n3368]Your [41] leave in this.[^n3369] [^n3370]And he touched the ear of him that was struck, and healed it. And in that hour Jesus said to the multitudes, As they come out against a thief are ye come out against me with swords and staves to take me? Daily was I with you in [42] the temple sitting teaching, and ye took me not: [^n3371]but this is your hour, and the power [43] of darkness. [^n3372]And that was, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. [44] [^n3373]Then the disciples all left him, and fled. And the footsoldiers and the officers [45] and the soldiers[^n3374] of the Jews seized Jesus, and came. [^n3375]And a certain[^n3376] young man [46] followed him, and he was wrapped in a towel, naked: [^n3377]and they seized him; so he [47] [Arabic, p. 184] left the towel, and fled naked. [^n3378]Then they took Jesus, and bound him, and brought him to Annas first; because he was the father in law of Caiaphas, [48] who was chief priest that year. [^n3379]And Caiaphas was he that counselled the Jews, that it was necessary that one man should die instead of the people. [49] [^n3380]And Simon Cephas and one of the other disciples followed Jesus. And the chief [50] priest knew that disciple, and he entered with Jesus into the court; [^n3381]but Simon was standing without at the door. And that other disciple, whom the chief priest knew, [51] went out and spake unto her that kept the door, and she brought Simon in. [^n3382]And when the maid that kept the door saw Simon, she looked stedfastly at him, and said unto him, Art not thou also one of the disciples of this man, I mean Jesus the [52] Nazarene? [^n3383]But he denied, and said, Woman, I know him not, neither know I even [53] what thou sayest. [^n3384]And the servants and the soldiers rose, and made a fire in the [54] middle of the court, that they might warm themselves; for it was cold. [^n3385]And when [55] the fire burned up, they sat down around it. [^n3386]And Simon also came, and sat down with them to warm himself, that he might see the end of what should happen.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section XLIX
text: Section XLIX. [1, 2] [^n3387]And the chief priest asked Jesus about his disciples, and about his doctrine.[^n3388] [^n3389]And Jesus said unto him, I was speaking[^n3390] openly to the people; and I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, where all the Jews gather; and I have spoken nothing in [3] [Arabic, p. 185] secret. [^n3391]Why askest thou me? ask those that have heard, what I spake unto [4] them: for they know all that I said. [^n3392]And when he had said that, one of the soldiers which were standing there struck the cheek[^n3393] of Jesus, and said unto him, [5] Dost thou thus answer the chief priest? [^n3394]Jesus answered and said unto him, If I [6] have spoken evil, bear witness of evil:[^n3395] but if well, why didst thou smite me? [^n3396]And Annas sent Jesus bound unto Caiaphas the chief priest. [7] [^n3397]And when Jesus went out, Simon Cephas was standing in the outer court warming [8] himself. [^n3398]And that maid saw him again, and began to say to those that stood [9] by, This man also was there with Jesus the Nazarene. [^n3399]And those that stood by [10] came forward and said to Cephas, Truly thou art one of his disciples. [^n3400]And he [11] denied again with an oath, I know not the man. [^n3401]And after a little one of the servants of the chief priest, the kinsman of him whose ear Simon cut off, saw him; and [12] he disputed[^n3402] and said, Truly this man was with him: [^n3403]and he also is a Galilæan; [13] and his speech resembles.[^n3404] [^n3405]And he said unto Simon, Did not I see thee with him [14] in the garden? [^n3406]Then began Simon to curse,[^n3407] and to swear, I know not this man [15] whom ye have mentioned. [^n3408]And immediately, while he was speaking, the cock crew [16] twice. [^n3409]And in that hour Jesus turned, he being without, and looked stedfastly at Cephas. And Simon remembered the word of our Lord, which he said unto him, [17, 18] [^n3410]Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. [^n3411]And Simon went forth without, and wept bitterly. [19] [Arabic, p. 186] [^n3412]And when the morning approached, the servants of all the chief priests and the scribes and the elders of the people and all the multitude assembled, [20, 21] and made a plot; [^n3413]and they took counsel against Jesus to put him to death. [^n3414]And they sought false witnesses who should witness against him, that they might put him to [22, 23] death, and they found not; [^n3415]but many false witnesses came, [^n3416]but their witness did not [24, 25] agree. [^n3417]But at last there came two lying witnesses, [^n3418]and said, We heard him say, I will destroy this[^n3419] temple of God that is made with hands, and will build another not [26, 27] made with hands after three days. [^n3420]And not even so did their witness agree. But Jesus was silent. [^n3421]And the chief priest rose in the midst, and asked Jesus, and said, [28] [^n3422]Answerest thou not a word concerning anything? what do these[^n3423] witness against [29, 30] thee? [^n3424]But Jesus was silent, and answered him nothing. [^n3425]And they took him up [31] into their assembly,[^n3426] and said unto him, If thou art the Messiah, tell us. [^n3427]He said [32] unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe me: [^n3428]and if I ask you, ye will not answer [33] me a word, nor let me go. [^n3429]And the chief priest answered and said unto him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou art the Messiah, the [34, 35] Son of the living God. [^n3430]Jesus said unto him, Thou hast said that I am he. [^n3431]They all said unto him, Then thou art now the Son of God? Jesus said, Ye have said [36] that I am he. [^n3432]I say unto you, that henceforth ye shall see the Son of man sitting [37] [Arabic, p. 187] at the right hand of power, and coming on the clouds of heaven. [^n3433]Then the [38] chief priest rent his tunic,[^n3434] and said, He hath blasphemed. [^n3435]And they all said, Why should we seek now witnesses? we have heard now the blasphemy from his mouth. [39, 40] What then think ye? [^n3436]They all answered and said, He is worthy of death. [^n3437]Then some of them drew near, and spat in his face, and struck him, and scoffed at him. [41] [^n3438]And the soldiers struck him on his cheeks,[^n3439] and said, Prophesy unto us, thou Messiah: [42] who is he that struck thee? [^n3440]And many other things spake they falsely,[^n3441] and said against him. [43] [^n3442]And all of their assembly arose,[^n3443] and took Jesus, and brought him bound[^n3444] to [44] the prætorium,[^n3445] and delivered him up to Pilate the judge; [^n3446]but they entered not into the prætorium, that they might not be defiled when they should eat the passover. [45] [^n3447]And Jesus stood before the judge. And Pilate went forth unto them without, and [46] said unto them, What accusation[^n3448] have ye against this man? [^n3449]They answered and said unto him, If he had not been doing evils, neither should we have delivered [47] him up unto thee. [^n3450]We found this man leading our people astray, and restraining from giving tribute to Cæsar, and saying of himself that he is the King, the Messiah. [48] [^n3451]Pilate said unto them, Then take ye him, and judge him according to your law. [Arabic, p. 188] The Jews said unto him, We have no authority to put a man to death: [49] [^n3452]that the word might be fulfilled, which Jesus spake, when he made known by what manner of death he was to die. [50] [^n3453]And Pilate entered into the prætorium, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art [51] thou the King of the Jews? [^n3454]Jesus said unto him, Of thyself saidst thou this, or [52] did others tell it thee concerning me? [^n3455]Pilate said unto him, Am I, forsooth,[^n3456] a Jew? The sons of thy nation[^n3457] and the chief priests delivered thee unto me: what [53] hast thou done? [^n3458]Jesus said unto him, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be [54] delivered to the Jews: now my kingdom is not from hence. [^n3459]Pilate said unto him, Then thou art a king? Jesus said unto him, Thou hast said that I am a king. And for this was I born, and for this came I into the world, that I should bear witness [55] of the truth. [^n3460]And every one that is of the truth heareth my voice. Pilate said unto him, And what is the truth? And when he said that, he went out again unto the Jews.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section L
text: Section L. [1] [^n3461]And Pilate said unto the chief priests and the multitude, I have not found [2] against this man anything. [^n3462]But they cried out and said, He hath disquieted[^n3463] our people with his teaching in all Judæa, and he began[^n3464] from Galilee and unto this [3] place. [^n3465]And Pilate, when he heard the name of Galilee, asked, Is this man a Galilæan? [4] [^n3466]And when he learned that he was under the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent him to Herod: for he was in Jerusalem in those days. [5] [^n3467]And Herod, when he saw Jesus, rejoiced exceedingly: for he had desired to see him for a long time, because he had heard regarding him many things; and he counted on[^n3468] [6] [Arabic, p. 189] seeing some sign from him. [^n3469]And he questioned him with many words; but [7] Jesus answered him not a word. [^n3470]And the scribes and chief priests were [8] standing by, and they accused him vehemently. [^n3471]And Herod scoffed at him, he and his servants; and when he had scoffed at him, he clothed him in robes of scarlet, [9] and sent him to Pilate. [^n3472]And on that day Pilate and Herod became friends, there having been[^n3473] enmity between them before that. [10, 11] [^n3474]And Pilate called the chief priests and the rulers of the people, [^n3475]and said unto them, Ye brought unto me this man, as the perverter of your people: and I have tried him before you, and have not found in this man any cause[^n3476] of all that ye [12] seek[^n3477] against him: [^n3478]nor yet Herod: for I sent him unto him; and he hath done [13] nothing for which he should deserve death. [^n3479]So now I will chastise him, and let [14, 15] him go. [^n3480]The multitude all cried out and said, Take him from us, take him. [^n3481]And [16] the chief priests and the elders accused him of many things. [^n3482]And during their [17] accusation he answered not a word. [^n3483]Then Pilate said unto him, Hearest thou not [18] how many things they witness against thee? [^n3484]And he answered him not, not even one word: and Pilate marvelled at that. [19] [^n3485]And when the judge sat on his tribune, his wife sent unto him, and said unto him, See that thou have nothing to do with that righteous man: for I have suffered much in my dream[^n3486] to-day because of him. [20] [^n3487]And at every feast the custom of the judge was to release to the people one [21] prisoner, him whom they would. [^n3488]And there was in their prison a well-known prisoner, [22, 23] called Barabbas. [^n3489]And when they assembled, Pilate said unto them, [^n3490]Ye have a custom, that I should release unto you a prisoner at the passover: will ye that I [24] release unto you the King of the Jews? [^n3491]And they all cried out and said, Release not [Arabic, p. 190] unto us this man, but release unto us Barabbas. And this Barabbas was a [25] robber, [^n3492]who for sedition[^n3493] and murder, which was in the city, was cast into the [26] prison. [^n3494]And all the people cried out and began to ask him to do as the custom was [27] that he should do with them. [^n3495]And Pilate answered and said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called the Messiah, the [28] King of the Jews? [^n3496]For Pilate knew that envy had moved them to deliver him up. [29] [^n3497]And the chief priests and the elders asked the multitudes to deliver Barabbas, and [30] to destroy Jesus. [^n3498]The judge answered and said unto them, Whom of the two will [31] ye that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas. [^n3499]Pilate said unto them, And [32] Jesus which is called the Messiah, what shall I do with him? [^n3500]They all cried out [33] and said, Crucify him. [^n3501]And Pilate spake to them again, for he desired to release [34] Jesus; [^n3502]but they cried out and said, Crucify him, crucify him, and release unto us [35] Barabbas. [^n3503]And Pilate said unto them a third time, What evil hath this man done? I have not found in him any cause[^n3504] to necessitate death: I will chastise him and [36] let him go. [^n3505]But they increased in importunity[^n3506] with a loud voice, and asked him to crucify him. And their voice, and the voice of the chief priests, prevailed. [37] [^n3507]Then Pilate released unto them that one who was cast into prison for sedition and murder, Barabbas, whom they asked for: [^n3508]and he scourged Jesus with whips.[^n3509] [38] [^n3510]Then the footsoldiers of the judge took Jesus, and went into the prætorium, and [39] [Arabic, p. 191] gathered unto him all of the footsoldiers. [^n3511]And they stripped him, and put on [40] him a scarlet cloak. [^n3512]And they clothed him in garments of purple, and plaited [41] a crown of thorns, and placed it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; [^n3513]and while they mocked at him and laughed, they fell down on their knees before him, and bowed [42] down to[^n3514] him, and said, Hail,[^n3515] King of the Jews! [^n3516]And they spat in his face, and took the reed from his hand, and struck him on his head, [^n3517]and smote his cheeks. [43] [^n3518]And Pilate went forth without again, and said unto the Jews, I bring him forth to [44] you, that ye may know that I do not find, in examining[^n3519] him, even one crime.[^n3520] [^n3521]And Jesus went forth without, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garments. [45] [^n3522]Pilate said unto them, Behold, the man! And when the chief priests and the soldiers[^n3523] saw him, they cried out and said, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate said unto them, Take him yourselves, and crucify him: for I find not a cause[^n3524] against [46] him. [^n3525]The Jews said unto him, We have a law, and according to our law he deserves [47] death, because he made himself the Son of God. [^n3526]And when Pilate heard this word, [48] his fear increased; [^n3527]and he entered again into the porch, and said to Jesus, Whence [49] art thou? [^n3528]But Jesus answered him not a word. Pilate said unto him, Speakest[^n3529] thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have authority to release thee, and have [50] authority to crucify thee? [^n3530]Jesus said unto him, Thou hast not any[^n3531] authority over me, if thou wert not given it from above: therefore the sin of him that delivered [51] me up unto thee is greater than thy sin. [^n3532]And for this word Pilate wished to release him: but the Jews cried out, If thou let him go, thou art not a friend of Cæsar: for every one that maketh himself a king is against Cæsar.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section LI
text: Section LI. [1] [Arabic, p. 192] [^n3533]And when Pilate heard this saying, he took Jesus out, and sat on the tribune in the place which was called the pavement of stones, but in the Hebrew [2] called Gabbatha. [^n3534]And that day was the Friday of the passover: and it had reached [3] about the sixth hour.[^n3535] [^n3536]And he said to the Jews, Behold, your King! And they cried out, Take him, take him, crucify him, crucify him. Pilate said unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests said unto him, We have no king except [4] Cæsar. [^n3537]And Pilate, when he saw it, and[^n3538] he was gaining nothing, but the tumult was increasing, took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, and said, I [5] am innocent of the blood of this innocent man: ye shall know.[^n3539] [^n3540]And all the people [6] answered and said, His blood be on us, and on our children. [^n3541]Then Pilate commanded to grant them their request; and delivered up Jesus to be crucified, according to their wish. [7] [^n3542]Then Judas the betrayer, when he saw Jesus wronged, went and returned the [8] thirty pieces of money to the chief priests and the elders, [^n3543]and said, I have sinned in my betraying innocent blood. And they said unto him, And we, what must we do? [9] know thou. [^n3544]And he threw down the money in the temple, and departed; and he [10] went away[^n3545] and hanged[^n3546] himself. [^n3547]And the chief priests took the money, and said, We have not authority to cast it into the place of the offering,[^n3548] for it is the price [11] of blood. [^n3549]And they took counsel, and bought with it the plain of the potter, for [12] the burial of strangers. [^n3550]Therefore that plain was called, The field of blood, unto [13] [Arabic, p. 193] this day. [^n3551]Therein[^n3552] was fulfilled the saying in the prophet which said, I took thirty pieces of money, the price of the precious one, which was fixed [14] by the children of Israel; [^n3553]and I paid them for the plain of the potter, as the Lord commanded me. [15] [^n3554]And the Jews took Jesus, and went away to crucify him. [^n3555]And when he bare his [16] cross and went out, they stripped him of those purple and scarlet garments which he [17] had on, and put on him his own garments. [^n3556]And while they were going with him, they found a man, a Cyrenian, coming from the country, named Simon, the father of Alexander and Rufus: [^n3557]and they compelled this man to bear the cross of Jesus. [18] [^n3558]And they took the cross and laid it upon him, that he might bear it, and come after Jesus; and Jesus went, and his cross behind him. [19] [^n3559]And there followed him much people, and women which were lamenting and [20] raving.[^n3560] [^n3561]But Jesus turned unto them and said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not [21] for me: weep for yourselves, and for your children. [^n3562]Days are coming, when they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that bare not, and the breasts [22] that gave not suck. [^n3563]Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and [23] to the hills, Cover us. [^n3564]For if they do so in the green tree,[^n3565] what shall be in the dry? [24] [^n3566]And they brought with Jesus two others of the malefactors,[^n3567] to be put to death. [25] [^n3568]And when they came unto a certain place called The skull, and called in the Hebrew Golgotha, they crucified him there: [^n3569]they crucified with him these two [26] malefactors, one on his right, and the other on his left. [^n3570]And the scripture was [27] [Arabic, p. 194] fulfilled, which saith, He was numbered with the transgressors. [^n3571]And they gave him to drink wine and myrrh, and vinegar which had been mixed with the myrrh; [^n3572]and he tasted, and would not drink; and he received it not. [28] [^n3573]And the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and cast lots for them in four parts, to every party of the soldiers a part; and his tunic was [29] without sewing, from the top woven throughout. [^n3574]And they said one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: and the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, They divided my garments among them, And cast the lot for my vesture. [30, 31] [^n3575]This the soldiers did. And they sat and guarded him there. [^n3576]And Pilate wrote on a tablet the cause of his death, and put it on the wood of the cross above his head.[^n3577] And there was written upon it thus: This is Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the [32] Jews. [^n3578]And this tablet[^n3579] read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city: and it was written in Hebrew and Greek and Latin. [33] [^n3580]And the chief priests said unto Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but, He it is [34] that[^n3581] said, I am the King of the Jews. [^n3582]Pilate said unto them, What hath been [35] written hath been written.[^n3583] [^n3584]And the people were standing beholding; and they [36] that passed by were reviling[^n3585] him, and shaking[^n3586] their heads, and saying, [^n3587]Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, [^n3588]save thyself if thou art the Son [37] of God, and come down from the cross. [^n3589]And in like manner the chief priests and the [Arabic, p. 195] scribes and the elders and the Pharisees derided him, and laughed one with [38, 39] another, and said, [^n3590]The saviour of others cannot save himself. [^n3591]If he is the Messiah, the chosen of God, and the King of Israel,[^n3592] let him come down now from the [40] cross, that we may see, and believe in him. [^n3593]He that relieth on God—let him deliver him [41] now, if he is pleased with him: for he said, I am the Son of God. [^n3594]And the soldiers [42] also scoffed at him in that they came near unto him, [^n3595]and brought him vinegar, and [43] said unto him, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself. [^n3596]And likewise the two robbers[^n3597] also that were crucified with him reproached him. [44] [^n3598]And one of those two malefactors who were crucified with him reviled him, and [45] said, If thou art the Messiah, save thyself, and save us also. [^n3599]But his comrade rebuked him, and said, Dost thou not even fear God, being thyself also in this [46] condemnation? [^n3600]And we with justice, and as we deserved, and according to our deed,[^n3601] have we been rewarded: but this man hath not done anything unlawful. [47] [^n3602]And he said unto Jesus, Remember me, my Lord, when thou comest in thy kingdom. [48] [^n3603]Jesus said unto him, Verily[^n3604] I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in Paradise. [49] [^n3605]And there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister,[^n3606] [50] Mary[^n3607] that was related to Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. [^n3608]And Jesus saw his mother, and that disciple whom he loved standing by; and he said to his mother, [51] Woman, behold, thy son! [^n3609]And he said to that disciple, Behold, thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto himself. [52] [Arabic, p. 196] [^n3610]And from the sixth hour[^n3611] darkness was on all the land unto the ninth [53] hour,[^n3612] and the sun became dark. [^n3613]And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and said, Yail, Yaili,[^n3614] why hast thou forsaken me? which[^n3615] is, My [54] God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? [^n3616]And some of those that stood there, when they heard, said,[^n3617] This man called Elijah.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section LII
text: Section LII. [1] [^n3618]And after that, Jesus knew that all things were finished; and that the scripture [2] might be accomplished, he said, I thirst. [^n3619]And there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and in that hour one of them hasted, and took a sponge, and filled it with that [3] vinegar, [^n3620]and fastened it on a reed, and brought it near[^n3621] his mouth to give him a [4] drink. [^n3622]And when Jesus had taken that vinegar, he said, Everything is finished. [5] [^n3623]But the rest said, Let be, that we may[^n3624] see whether Elijah cometh to save him. [6, 7] [^n3625]And Jesus said, My Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and said, My Father, into thy hands I commend[^n3626] my spirit. [^n3627]He said that, and bowed his head, and gave up his spirit. [8] [^n3628]And immediately the face of[^n3629] the door of the temple was rent into two parts from [9] top to bottom; [^n3630]and the earth was shaken; and the stones were split to pieces; and the [Arabic, p. 197] tombs were opened; and the bodies of many saints which slept, arose and [10] came forth; [^n3631]and after his resurrection they entered into the holy city and [11] appeared unto many. [^n3632]And the officer of the footsoldiers, and they that were with him who were guarding Jesus,[^n3633] when they saw the earthquake, and the things which came [12] to pass, feared greatly, and praised God, and said, [^n3634]This man was righteous; and, [13] Truly he was the Son of God. [^n3635]And all the multitudes that were come together to the sight, when they saw what came to pass, returned and smote upon their breasts. [14] [^n3636]And the Jews, because of the Friday, said, Let these bodies not remain on their crosses,[^n3637] because it is the morning of the sabbath (for that sabbath was a great day); and they asked of Pilate that they might break the legs of those that were [15] crucified, and take them down. [^n3638]And the soldiers came, and brake the legs of the [16] first, and that other which was crucified with him: [^n3639]but when they came to Jesus, [17] they saw that he had died before, so they brake not his legs: [^n3640]but one of the soldiers pierced[^n3641] him in his side with a spear, and immediately there came forth blood and [18] water. [^n3642]And he that hath seen hath borne witness, and his witness is true: and he [19] knoweth that he hath said the truth, that ye also may believe. [^n3643]This he did, that [20] the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, A bone shall not be broken in him; [^n3644]and the scripture also which saith, Let them look upon him whom they pierced.[^n3645] [21] [^n3646]And there were in the distance all the acquaintance of Jesus standing, and the women that came with him from Galilee, those that followed him and ministered. [22] [^n3647]One of them was Mary Magdalene; and Mary the mother of James the little and [23] [Arabic, p. 198] Joses, [^n3648]and the mother of the sons of Zebedee, and Salome, and many others which came up with him unto Jerusalem; [^n3649]and they saw that. [24] [^n3650]And when the evening of the Friday was come, because of the entering of the [25] sabbath, [^n3651]there came a rich man,[^n3652] a noble[^n3653] of Ramah,[^n3654] a city of Judah,[^n3655] named Joseph, and he was a good man and upright; [^n3656]and he was a[^n3657] disciple of Jesus, but [26] was concealing himself for fear of the Jews. [^n3658]And he did not agree with the accusers [27] in their desire and their deeds: [^n3659]and he was looking for the kingdom of God. [^n3660]And this man went boldly, and entered in unto Pilate, and asked of him the body of [28] Jesus. [^n3661]And Pilate wondered how he had died already: and he called the officer of [29] the footsoldiers, and asked him concerning his death before the time. [^n3662]And when [30] he knew, he commanded him to deliver up his body unto Joseph. [^n3663]And Joseph bought for him a winding cloth of pure linen, and took down the body of Jesus, [31] and wound it in it; and they came and took it. [^n3664]And there came unto him Nicodemus also, who of old came unto Jesus by night; and he brought with him perfume[^n3665] [32] of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds. [^n3666]And they took the body of Jesus, and wound it in the linen and the perfume, as was the custom of the Jews to bury. [33] [^n3667]And there was in the place where Jesus was crucified a garden; and in that garden [34] a new tomb cut out in a rock,[^n3668] wherein was never man yet laid. [^n3669]And they left [35] Jesus there because the sabbath had come in, and because the tomb was near. [^n3670]And they pushed[^n3671] a great stone, and thrust[^n3672] it against the door of the sepulchre, and [36] went away. [^n3673]And Mary Magdalene and Mary that was related to Joses came to [37] [Arabic, p. 199] the sepulchre after them,[^n3674] [^n3675]and sat opposite the sepulchre,[^n3676] and saw the [38] body, how they took it in and laid it there. [^n3677]And they returned, and bought ointment[^n3678] and perfume,[^n3679] and prepared[^n3680] it, that they might come and anoint him. [39] [^n3681]And on the day which was the sabbath day they desisted according to the command. [40, 41] [^n3682]And the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered unto Pilate, and said unto him, [^n3683]Our lord, we remember that that misleader said, while he was alive, After three days [42] I rise. [^n3684]And now send beforehand and guard the tomb[^n3685] until the third day,[^n3686] lest his disciples come and steal him by night, and they will say unto the people that he [43] is risen from the dead: and the last error shall be worse than the first. [^n3687]He said unto them, And have ye not guards?[^n3688] go, and take precautions as ye know how. [44] [^n3689]And they went, and set guards at the tomb, and sealed that stone, with the guards. [45] [^n3690]And in the evening of the sabbath, which is the morning of the first day, and in [46] the dawning[^n3691] while the darkness yet remained, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary and other women to see the tomb. [^n3692]They brought with them the [47] perfume which they had prepared, and said among themselves, [^n3693]Who is it that will [48] remove for us the stone from the door of the tomb? for it was very great. [^n3694]And when they said thus, there occurred a great earthquake; and an angel came down [49] from heaven, and came and removed the stone from the door. [^n3695]And they came and found the stone removed from the sepulchre, and the angel sitting upon the [50] stone. [^n3696]And his appearance was as the lightning, and his raiment white as the [51] snow: [^n3697]and for fear of him the guards were troubled, and became as dead men. [52] [^n3698]And when he went away, the women entered into the sepulchre; and they found [53] [Arabic, p. 200] not the body of Jesus. [^n3699]And they saw there a young man sitting on the [54] right, arrayed in a white garment; and they were amazed.[^n3700] [^n3701]And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear ye not: for I know that ye seek Jesus the [55] Nazarene, who hath been crucified. He is not here; but he is risen, as he said. [^n3702]Come and see the place where our Lord lay.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section LIII
text: Section LIII.[^n3703] [1] [^n3704]And while they marvelled at that, behold, two men standing above them, their [2] raiment shining: [^n3705]and they were seized with fright, and bowed down their face to [3] the earth: and they said unto them, Why seek ye the living one with the dead? [^n3706]He is not here; he is risen: remember what he was speaking unto you while he was in [4] Galilee, and saying, [^n3707]The Son of man is to be delivered up into the hands of sinners, [5] and to be crucified, and on the third day to rise. [^n3708]But go in haste, and say to his disciples and to Cephas, He is risen from among the dead; and lo, he goeth before [6] you into Galilee; [^n3709]and there ye shall see him, where[^n3710] he said unto you: lo, I have [7] told you. [^n3711]And they remembered his sayings; and they departed in haste from the [8] tomb with joy and great fear, and hastened and went; [^n3712]and perplexity and fear [9] encompassed them; and they told no man anything, for they were afraid. [^n3713]And Mary hastened, and came to Simon Cephas, and to that other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said unto them, They have taken our Lord from the sepulchre, and I [10] know not where they have laid him. [^n3714]And Simon went out, and that other disciple, [11] and came to the sepulchre. [^n3715]And they hastened both together: and that disciple [12] outran[^n3716] Simon, and came first to the sepulchre; [^n3717]and he looked down, and saw the [13] linen laid; but he went not in. [^n3718]And Simon came after him, and entered into the [14] [Arabic, p. 201] sepulchre, and saw the linen laid; [^n3719]and the scarf with which his head was bound was not with the linen, but wrapped and laid aside in a certain place. [15] [^n3720]Then entered that disciple which came first to the sepulchre, and saw, and believed. [16] [^n3721]And they knew not yet from the scriptures that the Messiah was to rise from among [17] the dead. [^n3722]And those two disciples went to their place. [18] [^n3723]But Mary remained[^n3724] at the tomb weeping: and while she wept, she looked [19] down into the tomb; [^n3725]and she saw two angels sitting in white raiment, one of them toward his pillow, and the other toward his feet, where the body of Jesus had been [20] laid. [^n3726]And they said unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She said unto them, [21] They have taken my Lord, and I know not where they have left him. [^n3727]She said that, and turned behind her, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was [22] Jesus. [^n3728]Jesus said unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? And she supposed[^n3729] him to be the gardener, and said, My lord, if thou hast taken him, [23] tell me where thou hast laid him, that I may go and take him. [^n3730]Jesus said unto her, Mary. She turned, and said unto him in Hebrew, Rabboni; which is, being [24] interpreted, Teacher. [^n3731]Jesus said unto her, Touch me not;[^n3732] for I have not ascended yet unto my Father: go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and my God and your God. [25] [^n3733]And on the First-day on which he rose, he appeared first unto Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons. [26] [^n3734]And some of those guards[^n3735] came to the city, and informed the chief priests of [27] [Arabic, p. 202] all that had happened. [^n3736]And they assembled with the elders, and took [28] counsel; [^n3737]and they gave money, not a little, to the guards, and said unto them, Say ye, His disciples came and stole him by night, while we were sleeping. [29] [^n3738]And if the judge hear that, we will make a plea with him, and free you of blame. [30] [^n3739]And they, when they took the money, did according to what they taught them. And this word spread among the Jews unto this day. [31] [^n3740]And then came Mary Magdalene, and announced to the disciples that she had seen our Lord, and that he had said that unto her. [32] [^n3741]And while the first[^n3742] women[^n3743] were going in the way to inform[^n3744] his disciples,[^n3745] [33] Jesus met them, and said unto them, Peace unto you. [^n3746]And they came and took [34] hold of his feet, and worshipped him. [^n3747]Then said Jesus unto them, Fear not: but go and say to my brethren that they depart into Galilee, and there they shall see [35] me. [^n3748]And those women returned, and told all that to the eleven, and to the rest of the disciples; [^n3749]and to those that had been with him, for they were saddened and [36] weeping. [^n3750]And those were Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and the rest who were with them: and they were those that told the apostles. [37] [^n3751]And they, when they heard them say that he was alive and had appeared unto them, [38] did not believe them: [^n3752]and these sayings were before their eyes as the sayings of madness. [39] [Arabic, p. 203] [^n3753]And after that, he appeared to two of them, on that day, and while they were going to the village which was named Emmaus, and whose distance [40] from Jerusalem was sixty furlongs.[^n3754] [^n3755]And they were talking the one of them with the [41] other of all the things which had happened. [^n3756]And during the time of their talking and [42] inquiring with one another, Jesus came and reached them, and walked with them. [^n3757]But [43] their eyes were veiled that they should not know him. [^n3758]And he said unto them, What are these sayings which ye address the one of you to the other, as ye walk and are [44] sad? [^n3759]One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said unto him, Art thou perchance alone a stranger to Jerusalem, since thou knowest not what was in [45] it in these days? He said unto them, What was? [^n3760]They said unto him, Concerning Jesus, he who was from Nazareth, a man who was a prophet, and powerful in [46] speech and deeds before God and before all the people: [^n3761]and the chief priests and [47] the elders delivered him up to the sentence of[^n3762] death, and crucified him. [^n3763]But we supposed that he was the one who was to deliver Israel. And since all[^n3764] these [48] things happened there have passed three days. [^n3765]But certain women of us also [49] informed us that they had come to the sepulchre; [^n3766]and when they found not his body, they came and told us that they had seen there the angels, and they[^n3767] said [50] concerning him that he was alive. [^n3768]And some of us also went to the sepulchre, and [51] found the matter as the women had said: only they saw him not. [^n3769]Then said Jesus [52] unto them, Ye lacking in discernment, and heavy in heart to believe! [^n3770]Was it not in all the sayings of the prophets that the Messiah was to suffer these things, and to [53] [Arabic, p. 204] enter into his Glory? [^n3771]And he began from Moses and from all the prophets, [54] and interpreted to them concerning himself from all the scriptures. [^n3772]And they drew near unto the village, whither they were going: and he was leading them to [55] imagine that he was as if going to a distant region. [^n3773]And they pressed[^n3774] him, and said unto him, Abide with us: for the day hath declined now to the darkness. And he went [56] in to abide with them. [^n3775]And when he sat with them, he took bread, and blessed, [57] and brake, and gave to them. [^n3776]And straightway their eyes were opened, and they [58] knew him; and he was taken away from them.[^n3777] [^n3778]And they said the one to the other, Was not our heart heavy within us, while he was speaking to us in the way, and interpreting to us the scriptures? [59] [^n3779]And they rose in that hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven [60] gathered, and those that were with them, saying, [^n3780]Truly our Lord is risen, and hath [61] appeared to Simon. [^n3781]And they related what happened in the way, and how they knew him when he brake the bread. [^n3782]Neither believed they that also.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section LIV
text: Section LIV. [1] [^n3783]And while they talked together,[^n3784] the evening of that day arrived which was the First-day; and the doors were shut where the disciples were, because of the fear of the [2] Jews; [^n3785]and Jesus came and stood among them, and said unto them, Peace be with you: I am he; fear not. [^n3786]But they were agitated, and became afraid, and supposed that they [3] saw a spirit. [^n3787]Jesus said unto them, Why are ye agitated? and why do thoughts rise [4] [Arabic, p. 205] in[^n3788] your hearts? [^n3789]See my hands and my feet, that I am he: feel me, and know that a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me having that. [5] [^n3790]And when he had said this, he shewed them his hands and his feet and his side.[^n3791] [6] [^n3792]And they were until this time unbelieving, from their joy and their wonder. He [7] said unto them, Have ye anything here to eat? [^n3793]And they gave him a portion of broiled fish and of honey.[^n3794] [^n3795]And he took it, and ate before them. [8] [^n3796]And he said unto them, These are the sayings which I spake unto you, while I was with you, that[^n3797] everything must be fulfilled, which is written in the law of [9] Moses, and the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me. [^n3798]Then opened he their [10] heart, that they might understand the scriptures; and he said unto them, [^n3799]Thus it is written, and thus it is necessary[^n3800] that the Messiah suffer, and rise from among the [11] dead on the third day; [^n3801]and that repentance unto the forgiveness of sins be preached [12] in his name among all the peoples; and the beginning shall be from Jerusalem. [^n3802]And [13] ye shall be witnesses of that. And I send unto you the promise of my Father. [^n3803]And [14] when the disciples heard that, they were glad. [^n3804]And Jesus said unto them again, [15] Peace be with you: as my Father hath sent me, I also send you. [^n3805]And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and said unto them, Receive ye the Holy Spirit: [16] [^n3806]and if ye forgive sins to any man, they shall be forgiven him; and if ye retain them against any man, they shall be retained. [17] [^n3807]But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Thama, was not there with the disciples [18] when Jesus came. [^n3808]The disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen our Lord. But he said unto them, If I do not see in his hands the places of the nails, and put on them my fingers, and pass my hand over his side, I will not believe. [19] [^n3809]And after eight days, on the next First-day, the disciples were assembled again within, and Thomas with them. And Jesus came, the doors being shut, and stood [20] [Arabic, p. 206] in the midst, and said unto them, Peace be with you. [^n3810]And he said to Thomas, Bring hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and bring hither [21] thy hand, and spread it on my side: and be not unbelieving, but believing. [^n3811]Thomas [22] answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God. [^n3812]Jesus said unto him, Now since thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen me, and have believed. [23] [^n3813]And many other signs did Jesus before his disciples, and they are they which [24] are not written in this book: [^n3814]but these that[^n3815] are written also are that ye may believe in Jesus the Messiah, the Son of God; and that when ye have believed, ye may have in his name eternal life. [25] [^n3816]And after that, Jesus shewed himself again to his disciples at the sea of Tiberias; [26] and he shewed himself unto them thus. [^n3817]And there were together Simon Cephas, and Thomas which was called Twin,[^n3818] and Nathanael who was of Cana of Galilee, [27] and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of the disciples. [^n3819]Simon Cephas said unto them, I go to catch fish. They said unto him, And we also come with thee. And they went forth, and went up into the boat; and in that night they caught nothing. [28] [^n3820]And when the morning arrived, Jesus stood on the shore of the sea: but the disciples [29] knew not that it was Jesus. [^n3821]And Jesus said unto them, Children, have ye anything [30] to eat? They said unto him, No. [^n3822]He said unto them, Cast your net from the right side of the boat, and ye shall find.[^n3823] And they threw, and they were not able [31] to draw the net for the abundance of the fish that were come[^n3824] into it. [^n3825]And that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Cephas, This is our Lord. And Simon, when he heard that it was our Lord, took his tunic, and girded it on his waist (for he was [32] naked), and cast himself into the sea to come to Jesus. [^n3826]But some others of the disciples came in the boat[^n3827] (and they were not far from the land, but about two [33] [Arabic, p. 207] hundred cubits), and drew that net of fish. [^n3828]And when they went up on the [34] land, they saw live coals laid, and fish laid thereon, and bread. [^n3829]And Jesus [35] said unto them, Bring of this fish which ye have now caught. [^n3830]Simon Cephas therefore went up, and dragged the net to the land, full of great fish, a hundred and fifty-three [36] fishes: and with all this weight that net was not rent. [^n3831]And Jesus said unto them, Come and sit down. And no man of the disciples dared to ask him who he was, for they knew that it was our Lord. But he did not appear to them in his own [37, 38] form. [^n3832]And Jesus came, and took bread and fish, and gave unto them. [^n3833]This is the third time that Jesus appeared to his disciples, when he had risen from among the dead. [39] [^n3834]And when they had breakfasted, Jesus said to Simon Cephas, Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me more than these? He said unto him, Yea, my Lord; thou [40] knowest that I love thee. [^n3835]Jesus said unto him, Feed for me my lambs. He said unto him again a second time, Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me? He said unto him, Yea, my Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He said unto him, Feed for [41] me my sheep.[^n3836] [^n3837]He said unto him again the third time, Simon, son of Jonah, lovest thou me? And it grieved Cephas that he said unto him three times, Lovest thou me? He said unto him, My Lord, thou knowest everything; thou knowest that I [42] love thee. [^n3838]Jesus said unto him, Feed for me my sheep.[^n3839] Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast a child, thou didst gird thy waist for thyself, and go whither [Arabic, p. 208] thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch out thy hands, and another shall gird thy waist, and take thee whither thou wouldest not. [43] [^n3840]He said that to him to explain by what death he was to glorify God. And when he [44] had said that, he said unto him, Come after me. [^n3841]And Simon Cephas turned, and saw that disciple whom Jesus loved following him; he which at the supper leaned[^n3842] on [45] Jesus’ breast, and said, My Lord, who is it that betrayeth thee? [^n3843]When therefore Cephas saw him, he said to Jesus, My Lord, and this man, what shall be in his [46] case?[^n3844] [^n3845]Jesus said unto him, If I will that this man remain until I come, what is [47] that to thee? follow thou me. [^n3846]And this word spread among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: but Jesus said not that he should not die; but, If I will that this man remain until I come, what is that to thee? [48] [^n3847]This is the disciple which bare witness of that, and wrote it: and we know that his witness is true.

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Section LV
text: Section LV. [1] [^n3848]But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain[^n3849] where Jesus had [2] appointed them. [^n3850]And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but there were of [3] them who doubted. [^n3851]And while they sat there he appeared to them again, and upbraided them for their lack of faith and the hardness of their hearts, those that saw him when he was risen, and believed not.[^n3852] [4] [Arabic, p. 209] [^n3853]Then said Jesus unto them, I have been given all authority in heaven [5] and earth; and as my Father hath sent me, so I also send you. [^n3854]Go now into [6] all the world, and preach my gospel in all the creation; [^n3855]and teach[^n3856] all the peoples, and [7] baptize them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit; [^n3857]and teach them to keep all whatsoever I commanded you: and lo, I am with you all the days, unto [8] the end of the world. [^n3858]For whosoever believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but [9] whosoever believeth not shall be rejected. [^n3859]And the signs[^n3860] which shall attend those that believe in me are these: that they shall cast out devils in my name; and they [10] shall speak with new tongues; [^n3861]and they shall take up serpents, and if they drink deadly poison,[^n3862] it shall not injure them; and they shall lay their hands on the diseased, [11] and they shall be healed. [^n3863]But ye, abide in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be clothed with power from on high. [12] [^n3864]And our Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, took them out to Bethany: and he [13] lifted up his hands, and blessed them. [^n3865]And while he blessed them, he was separated from them, and ascended into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God. [14, 15] [^n3866]And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy: [^n3867]and at all times they were in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen. [16] [^n3868]And from thence they went forth, and preached in every place; and our Lord helped them, and confirmed their sayings by the signs which they did.[^n3869] [17] [^n3870]And here are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they were written every one of them, not even the world, according to my opinion, would contain the books which should be written.[^n3871]

title: Tatian: Diatessaron — Arabic Witness
label: Subscriptions.
text: Subscriptions. I. In Borgian ms. Here endeth the Gospel which Tatianus compiled and named Diatessaron, i.e., The Fourfold, a compilation from the four Gospels of the holy Apostles, the excellent Evangelists (peace be upon them). It was translated by the excellent and learned priest, Abu’l Faraj ‘Abdulla ibn-at-Tayyib[^n3872] (may God grant him favour), from Syriac into Arabic, from an exemplar written by ‘Isa[^n3873] ibn-‘Ali al-Motatabbib,[^n3874] pupil of Honain ibn-Ishak (God have mercy on them both). Amen. 2. In Vatican ms.[^n3875] Here endeth, by the help of God, the holy Gospel that Titianus compiled from the four Gospels, which is known as Diatessaron. And praise be to God, as he is entitled to it and lord of it! And to him be the glory for ever.

title: Clement of Alexandria: The Instructor
label: Book I — Chapter I. The Office of the Instructor.
text: As there are these three things in the case of man, habits, actions, and passions; habits are the department appropriated by hortatory discourse the guide to piety, which, like the ship’s keel, is laid beneath for the building up of faith; in which, rejoicing exceedingly, and abjuring our old opinions, through salvation we renew our youth, singing with the hymning prophecy, “How good is God to Israel, to such as are upright in heart!”[^n1034] All actions, again, are the province of preceptive discourse; while persuasive discourse applies itself to heal the passions. It is, however, one and the self-same word which rescues man from the custom of this world in which he has been reared, and trains him up in the one salvation of faith in God. When, then, the heavenly guide, the Word, was inviting[^n1035] men to salvation, the appellation of hortatory was properly applied to Him: his same word was called rousing (the whole from a part). For the whole of piety is hortatory, engendering in the kindred faculty of reason a yearning after true life now and to come. But now, being at once curative and preceptive, following in His own steps, He makes what had been prescribed the subject of persuasion, promising the cure of the passions within us. Let us then designate this Word appropriately by the one name Tutor (or Pædagogue, or Instructor). The Instructor being practical, not theoretical, His aim is thus to improve the soul, not to teach, and to train it up to a virtuous, not to an intellectual life. Although this same word is didactic, but not in the present instance. For the word which, in matters of doctrine, explains and reveals, is that whose province it is to teach. But our Educator[^n1036] being practical, first exhorts to the attainment of right dispositions and character, and then persuades us to the energetic practice of our duties, enjoining on us pure commandments, and exhibiting to such as come after representations of those who formerly wandered in error. Both are of the highest utility,—that which assumes the form of counselling to obedience, and that which is presented in the form of example; which latter is of two kinds, corresponding to the former duality,—the one having for its purpose that we should choose and imitate the good, and the other that we should reject and turn away from the opposite. Hence accordingly ensues the healing of our passions, in consequence of the assuagements of those examples; the Pædagogue strengthening our souls, and by His benign commands, as by gentle medicines, guiding the sick to the perfect knowledge of the truth. There is a wide difference between health and knowledge; for the latter is produced by learning, the former by healing. One, who is ill, will not therefore learn any branch of instruction till he is quite well. For neither to learners nor to the sick is each injunction invariably expressed similarly; but to the former in such a way as to lead to knowledge, and to the latter to health. As, then, for those of us who are diseased in body a physician is required, so also those who are diseased in soul require a pædagogue to cure our maladies; and then a teacher, to train and guide the soul to all requisite knowledge when it is made able to admit the revelation of the Word. Eagerly desiring, then, to perfect us by a gradation conducive to salvation, suited for efficacious discipline, a beautiful arrangement is observed by the all-benignant Word, who first exhorts, then trains, and finally teaches.

title: Clement of Alexandria: The Instructor
label: Book I — Chapter II.—Our Instructor’s Treatment of Our Sins.
text: Now, O you, my children, our Instructor is like His Father God, whose son He is, sinless, blameless, and with a soul devoid of passion; God in the form of man, stainless, the minister of His Father’s will, the Word who is God, who is in the Father, who is at the Father’s right hand, and with the form of God is God. He is to us a spotless image; to Him we are to try with all our might to assimilate our souls. He is wholly free from human passions; wherefore also He alone is judge, because He alone is sinless. As far, however, as we can, let us try to sin as little as possible. For nothing is so urgent in the first place as deliverance from passions and disorders, and then the checking of our liability to fall into sins that have become habitual. It is best, therefore, not to sin at all in any way, which we assert to be the prerogative of God alone; next to keep clear of voluntary transgressions, which is characteristic of the wise man; thirdly, not to fall into many involuntary offences, which is peculiar to those who have been excellently trained. Not to continue long in sins, let that be ranked last. But this also is salutary to those who are called back to repentance, to renew the contest. And the Instructor, as I think, very beautifully says, through Moses: “If any one die suddenly by him, straightway the head of his consecration shall be polluted, and shall be shaved,”[^n1037] designating involuntary sin as sudden death. And He says that it pollutes by defiling the soul: wherefore He prescribes the cure with all speed, advising the head to be instantly shaven; that is, counselling the locks of ignorance which shade the reason to be shorn clean off, that reason (whose seat is in the brain), being left bare of the dense stuff of vice, may speed its way to repentance. Then after a few remarks He adds, “The days before are not reckoned irrational,”[^n1038] by which manifestly sins are meant which are contrary to reason. The involuntary act He calls “sudden,” the sin He calls “irrational.” Wherefore the Word, the Instructor, has taken the charge of us, in order to the prevention of sin, which is contrary to reason. Hence consider the expression of Scripture, “Therefore these things saith the Lord;” the sin that had been committed before is held up to reprobation by the succeeding expression “therefore,” according to which the righteous judgment follows. This is shown conspicuously by the prophets, when they said, “Hadst thou not sinned, He would not have uttered these threatenings.” “Therefore thus saith the Lord;” “Because thou hast not heard these words, therefore these things the Lord;” and, “Therefore, behold, the Lord saith.” For prophecy is given by reason both of obedience and disobedience: for obedience, that we may be saved; for disobedience, that we may be corrected. Our Instructor, the Word, therefore cures the unnatural passions of the soul by means of exhortations. For with the highest propriety the help of bodily diseases is called the healing art—an art acquired by human skill. But the paternal Word is the only Pæonian physician of human infirmities, and the holy charmer of the sick soul. “Save,” it is said, “Thy servant, O my God, who trusteth in Thee. Pity me, O Lord; for I will cry to Thee all the day.”[^n1039] For a while the “physician’s art,” according to Democritus, “heals the diseases of the body; wisdom frees the soul from passion.” But the good Instructor, the Wisdom, the Word of the Father, who made man, cares for the whole nature of His creature; the all-sufficient Physician of humanity, the Saviour, heals both body and soul. “Rise up,” He said to the paralytic; “take the bed on which thou liest, and go away home;”[^n1040] and straightway the infirm man received strength. And to the dead He said, “Lazarus, go forth;”[^n1041] and the dead man issued from his coffin such as he was ere he died, having undergone resurrection. Further, He heals the soul itself by precepts and gifts—by precepts indeed, in course of time, but being liberal in His gifts, He says to us sinners, “Thy sins be forgiven thee.”[^n1042] We, however, as soon as He conceived the thought, became His children, having had assigned us the best and most secure rank by His orderly arrangement, which first circles about the world, the heavens, and the sun’s circuits, and occupies itself with the motions of the rest of the stars for man’s behoof, and then busies itself with man himself, on whom all its care is concentrated; and regarding him as its greatest work, regulated his soul by wisdom and temperance, and tempered the body with beauty and proportion. And whatever in human actions is right and regular, is the result of the inspiration of its rectitude and order.

title: Clement of Alexandria: The Instructor
label: Book I — Chapter III.—The Philanthropy of the Instructor.
text: The Lord ministers all good and all help, both as man and as God: as God, forgiving our sins; and as man, training us not to sin. Man is therefore justly dear to God, since he is His workmanship. The other works of creation He made by the word of command alone, but man He framed by Himself, by His own hand, and breathed into him what was peculiar to Himself. What, then, was fashioned by Him, and after He likeness, either was created by God Himself as being desirable on its own account, or was formed as being desirable on account of something else. If, then, man is an object desirable for itself, then He who is good loved what is good, and the love-charm is within even in man, and is that very thing which is called the inspiration [or breath] of God; but if man was a desirable object on account of something else, God had no other reason for creating him, than that unless he came into being, it was not possible for God to be a good Creator, or for man to arrive at the knowledge of God. For God would not have accomplished that on account of which man was created otherwise than by the creation of man; and what hidden power in willing God possessed, He carried fully out by the forth-putting of His might externally in the act of creating, receiving from man what He made man;[^n1043] and whom He had He saw, and what He wished that came to pass; and there is nothing which God cannot do. Man, then, whom God made, is desirable for himself, and that which is desirable on his account is allied to him to whom it is desirable on his account; and this, too, is acceptable and liked. But what is loveable, and is not also loved by Him? And man has been proved to be loveable; consequently man is loved by God. For how shall he not be loved for whose sake the only-begotten Son is sent from the Father’s bosom, the Word of faith, the faith which is superabundant; the Lord Himself distinctly confessing and saying, “For the Father Himself loveth you, because ye have loved Me;”[^n1044] and again, “And hast loved them as Thou hast loved Me?”[^n1045] What, then, the Master desires and declares, and how He is disposed in deed and word, how He commands what is to be done, and forbids the opposite, has already been shown. Plainly, then, the other kind of discourse, the didactic, is powerful and spiritual, observing precision, occupied in the contemplation of mysteries. But let it stand over for the present. Now, it is incumbent on us to return His love, who lovingly guides us to that life which is best; and to live in accordance with the injunctions of His will, not only fulfilling what is commanded, or guarding against what is forbidden, but turning away from some examples, and imitating others as much as we can, and thus to perform the works of the Master according to His similitude, and so fulfil what Scripture says as to our being made in His image and likeness. For, wandering in life as in deep darkness, we need a guide that cannot stumble or stray; and our guide is the best, not blind, as the Scripture says, “leading the blind into pits.”[^n1046] But the Word is keen-sighted, and scans the recesses of the heart. As, then, that is not light which enlightens not, nor motion that moves not, nor loving which loves not, so neither is that good which profits not, nor guides to salvation. Let us then aim at the fulfilment of the commandments by the works of the Lord; for the Word Himself also, having openly become flesh,[^n1047] exhibited the same virtue, both practical and contemplative. Wherefore let us regard the Word as law, and His commands and counsels as the short and straight paths to immortality; for His precepts are full of persuasion, not of fear.

title: Clement of Alexandria: The Instructor
label: Book I — Chapter IV.—Men and Women Alike Under the Instructor’s Charge.
text: Let us, then, embracing more and more this good obedience, give ourselves to the Lord; clinging to what is surest, the cable of faith in Him, and understanding that the virtue of man and woman is the same. For if the God of both is one, the master of both is also one; one church, one temperance, one modesty; their food is common, marriage an equal yoke; respiration, sight, hearing, knowledge, hope, obedience, love all alike. And those whose life is common, have common graces and a common salvation; common to them are love and training. “For in this world,” he says, “they marry, and are given in marriage,”[^n1048] in which alone the female is distinguished from the male; “but in that world it is so no more.” There the rewards of this social and holy life, which is based on conjugal union, are laid up, not for male and female, but for man, the sexual desire which divides humanity being removed. Common therefore, too, to men and women, is the name of man. For this reason I think the Attics called, not boys only, but girls, παιδάριον, using it as a word of common gender; if Menander the comic poet, in Rhapizomena, appears to any one a sufficient authority, who thus speaks:— “My little daughter; for by nature The child (παιδάριον) is most loving. Ἄρνες, too, the word for lambs, is a common name of simplicity for the male and female animal. Now the Lord Himself will feed us as His flock forever. Amen. But without a sheperd, neither can sheep nor any other animal live, nor children without a tutor, nor domestics without a master.”

title: Clement of Alexandria: The Instructor
label: Book I — Chapter V.—All Who Walk According to Truth are Children of God.
text: That, then, Pædagogy is the training of children (παίδων ἀγωγή), is clear from the word itself. It remains for us to consider the children whom Scripture points to; then to give the pædagogue charge of them. We are the children. In many ways Scripture celebrates us, and describes us in manifold figures of speech, giving variety to the simplicity of the faith by diverse names. Accordingly, in the Gospel, “the Lord, standing on the shore, says to the disciples”—they happened to be fishing—“and called aloud, Children, have ye any meat?”[^n1049]—addressing those that were already in the position of disciples as children. “And they brought to Him,” it is said, “children, that He might put His hands on them and bless them; and when His disciples hindered them, Jesus said, Suffer the children, and forbid them not to come to Me, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.”[^n1050] What the expression means the Lord Himself shall declare, saying, “Except ye be converted, and become as little chidren, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven;”[^n1051] not in that place speaking figuratively of regeneration, but setting before us, for our imitation, the simplicity that is in children.[^n1052] The prophetic spirit also distinguishes us as children. “Plucking,” it is said, “branches of olives or palms, the children went forth to meet the Lord, and cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord;”[^n1053] light, and glory, and praise, with supplication to the Lord: for this is the meaning of the expression Hosanna when rendered in Greek. And the Scripture appears to me, in allusion to the prophecy just mentioned, reproachfully to upbraid the thoughtless: “Have ye never read, Out of the mouths of babes and sucklings Thou hast perfected praise?”[^n1054] In this way the Lord in the Gospels spurs on His disciples, urging them to attend to Him, hastening as He was to the Father; rendering His hearers more eager by the intimation that after a little He was to depart, and showing them that it was requisite that they should take more unsparing advantage of the truth than ever before, as the Word was to ascend to heaven. Again, therefore, He calls them children; for He says, “Children, a little while I am with you.”[^n1055] And, again, He likens the kingdom of heaven to children sitting in the market-places and saying, “We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned, and ye have not lamented;”[^n1056] and whatever else He added agreeably thereto. And it is not alone the Gospel that holds these sentiments. Prophecy also agrees with it. David accordingly says, “Praise, O children, the Lord; praise the name of the Lord.”[^n1057] It says also by Esaias, “Here am I, and the children that God hath given me.”[^n1058] Are you amazed, then, to hear that men who belong to the nations are sons in the Lord’s sight? You do not in that case appear to give ear to the Attic dialect, from which you may learn that beautiful, comely, and freeborn young maidens are still called παιδίσκαι, and servant-girls παιδισκάρια; and that those last also are, on account of the bloom of youth, called by the flattering name of young maidens. And when He says, “Let my lambs stand on my right,”[^n1059] He alludes to the simple children, as if they were sheep and lambs in nature, not men; and the lambs He counts worthy of preference, from the superior regard He has to that tenderness and simplicity of disposition in men which constitutes innocence. Again, when He says, “as suckling calves,” He again alludes figuratively to us; and “as an innocent and gentle dove,”[^n1060] the reference is again to us. Again, by Moses, He commands “two young pigeons or a pair of turtles to be offered for sin;”[^n1061] thus saying, that the harmlessness and innocence and placable nature of these tender young birds are acceptable to God, and explaining that like is an expiation for like. Further, the timorousness of the turtle-doves typifies fear in reference to sin. And that He calls us chickens the Scripture testifies: “As a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings.”[^n1062] Thus are we the Lord’s chickens; the Word thus marvellously and mystically describing the simplicity of childhood. For sometimes He calls us children, sometimes chickens, sometimes infants, and at other times sons, and “a new people,” and “a recent people.” “And my servants shall be called by a new name”[^n1063] (a new name, He says, fresh and eternal, pure and simple, and childlike and true), which shall be blessed on the earth. And again, He figuratively calls us colts unyoked to vice, not broken in by wickedness; but simple, and bounding joyously to the Father alone; not such horses “as neigh after their neighbours’ wives, that are under the yoke, and are female-mad;”[^n1064] but free and new-born, jubilant by means of faith, ready to run to the truth, swift to speed to salvation, that tread and stamp under foot the things of the world. “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion; tell aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh, just, meek, and bringing salvation; meek truly is He, and riding on a beast of burden, and a young colt.”[^n1065] It was not enough to have said colt alone, but He added to it also young, to show the youth of humanity in Christ, and the eternity of simplicity, which shall know no old age. And we who are little ones being such colts, are reared up by our divine colt-tamer.
